question.problem:
Given that the function

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{x}{2}-b), & 2<x\le 4 \\ 4-x, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

 
is continuous at  $x=4,$ find the value of $b.$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=4,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}g(x) & =g(4) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{2}-b) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2-b),\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}(4-x) \\  & =4-4 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=4,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}g(x) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(2-b) & =0 \\ 2-b & =1 \\ b & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
